title: 4 Days in Mexico City: Tacos, Markets & Hidden Gems
description: Your personalized Mexico City itinerary with specific restaurants, hidden gems, and local tips.

days.title: Ancient Ruins, Street Tacos & Mezcal
days.description: Your first day is about the historic core — Aztec ruins, colonial grandeur, and some of the best street food on the planet.

activities.name: Explore the Heart of the City
activities.description: Start at the Zócalo, one of the world's largest public plazas. Walk into the Palacio Nacional (free, bring ID) to see Diego Rivera's epic murals spanning Mexican history. Then head next door to Templo Mayor — the excavated main temple of the Aztec capital Tenochtitlán, sitting right in the middle of the modern city.

activities.name: Palacio de Bellas Artes & Mercado San Juan
activities.description: Walk to the jaw-dropping Palacio de Bellas Artes — even if you skip the museum, the Art Nouveau/Art Deco building itself is stunning. Then head to Mercado San Juan, the city's legendary gourmet market. This is where chefs shop — you'll find imported cheeses, exotic meats, and incredible seafood tostadas.

activities.name: Mezcal, Views & Los Cocuyos
activities.description: Head to Balcón del Zócalo for sunset drinks on the terrace overlooking the cathedral and the lit-up Zócalo. Then walk to Los Cocuyos, the legendary late-night taco stand that's been serving beef tongue, tripe, and suadero since the 1950s.

days.title: Coffee, Art Deco & Al Pastor
days.description: Today you explore Mexico City's trendiest neighborhoods — tree-lined streets, world-class restaurants, and the best al pastor trompo in the city.

activities.name: Roma Norte Coffee Culture
activities.description: Start with coffee at Chiquitito Café, a tiny beloved spot in Roma Norte, then stroll down tree-lined Álvaro Obregón with its sculptures and fountains. Pop into Librería Rosario Castellanos (a gorgeous two-story bookshop) and explore the side streets — Roma Norte rewards wanderers.

activities.name: Art Deco Architecture & Park Life
activities.description: Walk into Condesa and spend the afternoon wandering Parque México — watch the dogs, sit by the fountain, admire the Art Deco buildings along Avenida México. Stop at Churrería El Moro for churros and hot chocolate (a 90-year-old chain that's still perfect).

activities.name: The Al Pastor Trompo Trail
activities.description: Tonight is about one thing: finding your al pastor soulmate. Start at Taquería Orinoco for a fun, lively atmosphere and excellent pastor. Then walk to El Vilsito — a mechanic shop by day, taco stand by night. This is the real CDMX experience.

days.title: Frida, Floating Gardens & Pulque
days.description: Adventure day — you'll visit Frida Kahlo's blue house, float through ancient Aztec canals on a trajinera, and discover the bohemian soul of Coyoacán.

activities.name: Frida Kahlo Museum & Mercado de Coyoacán
activities.description: Book your Casa Azul (Frida Kahlo Museum) tickets online in advance — they sell out. The blue house is intimate and moving. After, wander the cobblestone streets of Coyoacán to the Mercado de Coyoacán for tostadas and fresh juices. Don't miss the Jardín Centenario plaza with its coyote fountain.

activities.name: Trajinera Ride on Ancient Canals
activities.description: Uber to Xochimilco's Embarcadero Nativitas. Hire a trajinera (colorful flat-bottom boat) and float through the canals — vendors in smaller boats will come to you selling corn, beer, flowers, and even mariachi. This is pure magic. Budget 2–3 hours.

activities.name: Pulque & Coyoacán Nightlife
activities.description: Head back to Coyoacán for the evening. Visit La Bipo, a lively pulquería where you can try curados (fruit-flavored pulque). Then for a more refined nightcap, try Pare de Sufrir — a mezcalería hidden behind an unmarked door.

days.title: Museum, Castle & Farewell Feast
days.description: Your final day mixes world-class culture with upscale dining — the Anthropology Museum, Chapultepec Castle, and Polanco's best restaurants.

activities.name: The World's Greatest Anthropology Museum
activities.description: This is Mexico's most-visited museum for good reason. The Aztec Sun Stone, the Maya jade masks, the Olmec heads — it's overwhelming in the best way. Focus on the Mexica (Aztec) and Maya halls if you're short on time. Budget 2–3 hours minimum.

activities.name: Castle Views & Upscale Strolling
activities.description: Walk uphill to Chapultepec Castle — the only royal castle in the Americas. The panoramic views of Paseo de la Reforma and the city are incredible. Then stroll through Polanco's leafy streets — window-shop on Av. Presidente Masaryk and visit Museo Soumaya (free, incredible art collection in a futuristic building).

activities.name: Last Night in CDMX
activities.description: For your final evening, head back to Roma for one last walk. End at Esquina Común, a magical rooftop dining experience in Condesa — or keep it casual with one more round of al pastor at your new favorite taquería.
